Q: PHPNative: New Android application A:

It's not perfectly clear to me what you did there.

You said that:

I've made a clean build of PHPNative (https://github.com/lyskouski/app-game-fantasyland)

So what I read is that you created the project with these steps:

composer create-project laravel/laravel .
composer require nativephp/mobile
php artisan native:install
php artisan native:run

And then you created a git repo that you pushed on github.

By reading the logs you shared all I can see is that the native:install step completed without errors but failed to generate the bootstrap file vendor/nativephp/mobile/bootstrap/android/native.php, so when native:run tried to include it, PHP threw a fatal "failed opening required" error.

It's hard to say why that happened because maybe some details are missing.

By the way I just cloned your repo as is and followed a very exact set of steps and the application could successfully run on the device emulator running from Android Studio.

You may try to follow those exact steps starting from a fresh dir and maybe you will later comment if you had further errors following my same procedure. Some steps are slightly different from yours because I didn't start from the same state you have with files not tracked by the git repo.

1. Cloning the repo

git clone https://github.com/lyskouski/app-game-fantasyland.git
cd app-game-fantasyland

2. composer install

composer install
copy .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate

Those steps were not required in your case since we suppose you were working on a dir where you did:

composer create-project laravel/laravel .

3. Native PHP configuration in .env file

https://nativephp.com/docs/mobile/3/getting-started/configuration

Add the following lines in the .env file we copied in the previous step:

NATIVEPHP_APP_ID=com.tercad.fantasyland
NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION=1.0.0
NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE=1

This is something still referring to the .env file that you supposedly already had and it's out of the scope of the git repo and why you didn't include in your original procedure.

4. Deploy to Android

php artisan native:install
php artisan native:run

Q: How to sync a Python List of Canvas IDs with canvas.delete("all") to avoid errors in an Undo function? A:

I've been meaning to make a graphical Undo/Redo/Clrdo program for some time so here is my solution.

I've kept the drawing method (it's really inefficient) since a line can contain hundreds of points. It would be more efficient to draw multi-point lines and polygons or two point rectangles or ovals.

HOW IT WORKS:

Two lists called 'undoList' and 'redoList' hold all references to drawn objects. There's no need for any index pointer since all items are 'popped' from one list and 'pushed' onto the other.

Drawing lines is simply a matter of dragging the mouse with `Button-1` pressed. Deleting items is achieved by moving the pointer over drawing and pressing `Button-3`.

Using `Control-z` for undo and `Control-Z` for redo are standard methods of control.

To avoid using global I've created class store with the instance name the.

import tkinter as tk
import random

root = tk.Tk()

class store:
    history = False
    xx = yy = 0
    item = 0

    def color(self):
        return random.choice(["red", "blue", "green", "black"])

    def make_history(self):
        self.history = True
        self.redoList = []
        self.undoList = []

the = store()

def updateCoords(event):
    the.xx, the.yy = event.x, event.y

def drawLine(event):
    the.line_id = the.canvas.create_line(
        the.xx, the.yy, event.x, event.y, fill=the.color(), width=3)
    the.undoList.append(the.line_id)
    updateCoords(event)

def undo(event):
    if len(the.undoList) > 0:
        the.item = the.undoList.pop(~0)
        the.redoList.append(the.item)
        the.canvas.itemconfig(the.item, state = "hidden")

def redo(event):
    if len(the.redoList) > 0:
        the.item = the.redoList.pop(~0)
        the.undoList.append(the.item)
        the.canvas.itemconfig(the.item, state = "normal")

def clrdo(event):
    the.xx, the.yy = event.x, event.y    
    the.item = (the.canvas.find_closest(the.xx, the.yy) + (0,))[0]
    if the.item:
        if the.redoList.count(the.item) > 0:
            the.redoList.remove(the.item)
            the.canvas.delete(the.item)
        elif the.undoList.count(the.item) > 0:
            the.undoList.remove(the.item)
            the.canvas.delete(the.item)
        else:
            print(the.item)

def focus(event):
    the.canvas.focus_set()

def makecanvas(event = None):
    the.make_history() 
    the.canvas = tk.Canvas(
        root, takefocus = 1, width=400, height=300,
        cursor = "tcross", background="white")
    the.canvas.grid(row=0, column = 0, sticky = tk.NSEW)
    for a, b in [
        ("<Button-1>", updateCoords), ("<ButtonRelease-3>", clrdo),
        ("<B1-Motion>", drawLine), ("<Control-Z>", redo), ("<Control-z>", undo),
        ("<KeyRelease-Escape>", clearCanvas), ("<Enter>", focus)]:

        the.canvas.bind(a, b)

    root.rowconfigure(0, weight = 1)
    root.columnconfigure(0, weight=1)

def clearCanvas(event=None):
    the.canvas.destroy()
    makecanvas()

makecanvas()
root.mainloop()

Q: Why does my react tests fail in CI-pipeline due to "not wrapped in act()", while working fine locally? A:

The issue happens because async state updates continue after the test has “finished”. Locally, timing hides it. In CI, slower CPUs and concurrency expose updates that React sees as outside act().

Why the act() Warnings Happen

React requires that all state updates triggered by your test happen inside act().

Testing Library automatically wraps userEvent for you.

If something schedules a state update after your awaited findAllByRole resolves, React will warn:

not wrapped in act()

And if something else tries to wrap again while an update is already in progress:

nested calls to act() are not supported

That’s usually a symptom of overlapping async updates, not incorrect manual act() usage.

How to Debug This Systematically

Instead of chasing individual warnings, try to identify:

  • What async work is still active when the test ends?

  • Are there timers?

  • Are there unresolved promises?

  • Are effects triggered after the last assertion?

You can enforcing async cleanup at test boundaries and flakey test detection using jest-doctor

Summary

  • With modern user-events all functions return promises which need to be awaited, if they are not awaited later tests can cause errors

  • Use eslint to detect floating promises

  • Ensure MSW handlers are not resolving after the test moves forward.

Q: Export plotly to powerpoint in R A:

Powerpoint is no webviewer. Thus implementing a Plotly.js chart that bases on d3.js as interactive plot is very tricky. I struggle to find a proper usecase for this and would recommend to just create a presentation using Quarto + Reveal.js. Still, here is a way for Windows 11:

  1. Create a manifest.xml file in folder C:\ppt_manifest\. Herein set SourceLocation as "http://127.0.0.1:4321"

xsi:type="ContentApp" --> makes it a movable window

See <DefaultSettings>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<OfficeApp xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/appforoffice/1.1"
           xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
           xsi:type="ContentApp">
  <Id>d1919f0a-3d6a-44d7-8d64-e8328ca9531a</Id>
  <Version>1.0.0.0</Version>
  <ProviderName>You</ProviderName>
  <DefaultLocale>en-US</DefaultLocale>
  <DisplayName DefaultValue="Web Viewer" />
  <Description DefaultValue="View any http URL in task pane" />
  <Hosts>
    <Host Name="Presentation" />
  </Hosts>
  <DefaultSettings>
    <SourceLocation DefaultValue="http://127.0.0.1:6858" />
    <RequestedWidth>500</RequestedWidth>
    <RequestedHeight>400</RequestedHeight>
  </DefaultSettings>
  <Permissions>ReadWriteDocument</Permissions>
</OfficeApp>

Right-click the C:\ppt_manifest\ folder -> Properties -> Sharing -> Share it and note the network path it gives you, i.e. \\DESKTOP-0U5B5UM\ppt_manifest.

In PowerPoint: Options -> Trust Center -> Trust Center Settings -> Trusted Add-in Catalogs. Paste the share network UNC-path i.e. \\DESKTOP-0U5B5UM\ppt_manifest -> Add Catalog -> check "Show in Menu" -> OK.

  1. Restart PowerPoint.

  2. In R, serve your plotly on a server

library(plotly)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(servr)  # install.packages("servr")

p <- plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
saveWidget(p, "D:/Dokumente/R/Plotly in Powerpoint/chart.html", selfcontained = TRUE)

servr::httd("D:/Dokumente/R/Plotly in Powerpoint") # Serve the folder on localhost

# To stop the server, run servr::daemon_stop(1) or restart your R session
# Serving the directory D:\Dokumente\R\Plotly in Powerpoint at http://127.0.0.1:4321

  1. Open your Add-In: Developer (If "Developer Tab" is missing: On the File tab, go to Options > Customize Ribbon. Under Customize the Ribbon and under Main Tabs, select the Developer check box.) -> Add-Ins -> Shared Folder -> "Web Viewer" (or whatever your DisplayName DefaultValue is)

  2. Navigate to your plotly chart.html.

  • To host a shiny app, update SourceLocation-link to the one in "Listening on http:"
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

# Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5945 <-- this one
  • If you save the ppt once, the side window pane will stay. You can first host the server, then open the ppt using 1 or 2. Using Shiny you can make a fully fletched Powerpoint-UI and backend with R.

R or any other programming language

--> Perhaps https://pypi.org/project/plotlyPowerpoint/?

Q: What is the `tr` command in Windows? A:

In PowerShell, I used the -replace operator to emulate tr.

In my case, I wanted to replace all non-alphanumeric characters with underscores:

$original = "ÄÖ Clean this up ÄÖ"
$cleaned = $original -replace '[^a-zA-Z0-9]', '_'

See also this.

Q: Zip arrays in JavaScript? A:

There will be dedicated function in the near future! There is stage 3 draft of Iterator.zip() function which do exactly what you want:

const a = [1, 2, 3]
const b = ["a", "b", "c"]

Iterator.zip([a, b]).toArray();

// > [[1, "a"], [2, "b"], [3, "c"]]

link to MDN (docs). At the bottom of the page you can see current adoption and links to polyfills that already implement it (core-js, es-shims)

The draft also define Iterator.zipKeyed() which work similarly but outputs objects instead of lists.

Q: mat data type = 17 is not supported A:

This has been fixed a few years ago. Now you get a useful error message.

The situation is simple: imread() returned None, not an array.

cvtColor(), given None, would have complained that the array is empty. OpenCV implicitly converts None to an empty array (cv::Mat).

But then you had to needlessly convert the return value from imread into a numpy array. That gave you a zero-dimensional numpy array of dtype=object, to hold the None value.

cvtColor() given an array of dtype=object then used to complain about src data type = 17, which was misleading.

There is not actually any cv::Mat/array of element type 17 involved. CV_8SC3 would have the value 17, but that's not it.

Since July of 2023, it would instead say in this:

> Overload resolution failed:
>  - src data type = object is not supported
  • Issue: Python bindings: Overload resolution failed, "data type = 17", should be called out as numpy array of dtype=object #23106
  • PR: feat: update NumPy type to Mat type fail message #23958
